# Fast tensor convolution by core blocks and sparse face corrections

This gives a constructive replacement for g dense halo scans. It applies to
a **translation-invariant separable compact stencil**, with optional
diagonal conjugations whose coefficients and tile gauges satisfy the
precision and sequential-access conditions below. It does not claim that
the separate Gaussian product-tree factorization has this form.

Let g consecutive active axes have dyadic lengths S_i, with
`h=max_i log2 S_i`. Earlier coordinates are outer prefix fibers. Later
coordinates are a complete payload R, so they need no keys or transposition.
Let V denote the total bit volume, including B-bit coefficient records and
all spectators. Assume B=Theta(p), `g h=O(p)`, and the active group grows
superpolynomially. A fixed number of tapes may hold O(V) bits.

The operation is

```
(Tf)(x) = sum_{z in [-L,L]^g} [product_i k_i(z_i)] f(x-z mod S),
```

where `L=poly(p)`. A fixed or polylogarithmic number of these operations and
diagonal scans is allowed. Kernel coefficients, coefficient products and
the required intermediates have O(p)-bit representations under the supplied
normalization contract. The retained grouped convolution engine on a
binary field of width k has cost `O(V k^(1-q) polylog p)`. Polynomial-length
one-axis convolution also has its unconditional quasilinear bit algorithm;
it does not invoke the improved bound being proved.

Choose a dyadic tile side N dividing every S_i, with `N>4L` and `gL/N=o(1)`.
Write `b=log2 N`, `k=gb`, and `K0=O(g(h+b)+log g)=O(gh)` for a correction key.
Require `K0^2=O(B)` or retain the explicit extra metadata term below.

The complete cost is

```
O(V [ (gb)^(1-a) polylog p
      + (gb)^(1-q) polylog p
      + polylog p
      + (gL/N) (K0 + g polylog p) ])
+ polynomial(p) setup,
```

plus `O((gL/N)V K0^2/B)` if metadata arithmetic is not absorbed by records.
All scans, duplication, sparse sorts, local transposes and final output
order are included. In particular, there is no gV layout term.

## 1. One support-limited gather

Within the active group, gather its g low b-bit fields into a contiguous
suffix using the support-at-most-2gb extension proved in
`SUPPORT-ROUTER.md`. The remaining active coarse bits remain in their
possibly scrambled order. Every coarse tile is now one contiguous block
of N^g complete R-payloads. No other active coarse bit is put into a new
stable order, and no spectator coordinate is gathered.

The initial and inverse gather together cost
`O(V (gb)^(1-a) polylog p)`. The explicit permutation maps each physical
coarse tile name back to its logical vector; that small map is used only
for tile setup and sparse correction metadata.

## 2. Interior outputs from ordinary cyclic convolution

Flatten a tile by `phi(x)=sum_i x_i N^(g-1-i)` into Q=N^g slots. Put the
product kernel at offsets `psi(z)=sum_i z_i N^(g-1-i) mod Q` in an ordinary
one-dimensional cyclic convolution kernel. These offsets are distinct:
reduce a putative collision modulo N, use `2L<N`, then repeat for successive
digits. The dense Q-slot kernel can be generated by a zero scan plus sorted
sparse product coefficients. Its `(2L+1)^g` nonzero coefficients and their
polynomial metadata are negligible compared with Q in the stated regime
`N/L >= p^eta`, `g -> infinity`; alternatively a supplied sequential dense
kernel generator is an explicit acceptable input.

If every tile coordinate satisfies `L<=x_i<N-L`, then every `x_i-z_i` lies
in `[0,N)`. No mixed-radix carry or borrow occurs. Hence

```
phi(x)-psi(z) = phi(x-z) mod Q
```

uses precisely the intended same-tile input. Keep these interior outputs.
Discard the remaining outputs, whose carries can be wrong. This is why no
identification of cyclic and tensor convolution is made at a boundary.

The grouped convolution cost is
`O(V (g log N)^(1-q) polylog p)`, with no per-axis doubling or padding.

## 3. Disjoint face partition and exact halo volume

Partition boundary outputs by their **first** boundary axis j, and by low
or high side. For one output tile, the corresponding output rectangle has
intervals

```
i<j: [L,N-L)
i=j: [0,L) or [N-L,N)
i>j: [0,N).
```

These 2g rectangles are disjoint and contain every discarded output once.
Their required unwrapped input rectangles have intervals

```
i<j: [0,N)
i=j: [-L,2L) or [N-2L,N+L)
i>j: [-L,N+L).
```

Coordinates outside `[0,N)` are taken from the correct neighboring coarse
tile, including periodic wrap in each actual axis. All input dimensions
are less than 2N; no assumption of independent full 2N padding is used.

The total copied input volume is exactly

```
M = 6L V/N^g * sum_{j=0}^{g-1} N^j (N+2L)^(g-1-j)
  = 3V [ (1+2L/N)^g - 1 ]
  = O((gL/N)V).
```

The corrected output volume is
`V [1-(1-2L/N)^g] = O((gL/N)V)`. The formulas count corner duplication
exactly. An individual corner may have many destinations; its total traffic
is already included in M. No bound by worst-case 2^g multiplicity is charged
to all records.

## 4. One full scan generates all correction copies

For each original core tile, recover its logical coarse coordinates once.
Scan its local coordinate tuple with a binary odometer. Maintain flags for
membership in the four fixed edge intervals `[0,L)`, `[0,2L)`,
`[N-2L,N)` and `[N-L,N)`. Only coordinates changed by the odometer update
their flags. The number of coordinate updates over a whole tile is
`Q(1+1/N+...)<2Q`. Comparisons cost O(log N), and counters/head resets use
the retained amortized stream-counter convention. Maintain a count of
active near-boundary flags. A nonexceptional record takes no scan through
the g flags.

For an exceptional record, enumerate candidate first-boundary axes from
the flag tape and all valid neighboring-tile choices. The exact choices
are the ones implemented in `sparse_copies` in `check_halo.py`: earlier
axes stay in the original tile; the selected face axis has its own or one
adjacent tile; each later axis has its own tile plus an adjacent tile only
when within L of that edge. Every emitted record carries

```
(j, side, destination coarse tile, unwrapped local coordinates).
```

These are K0=O(gh) bits. Precompute the plus/minus-one forms of each logical
coarse coordinate once per tile. A copy's logical neighbor is generated
by selecting those forms, then encoding the known scrambled coarse order.
All carries, periodic wraps and changed tile order are explicit. Using
ordinary binary arithmetic gives O(K0^2) safe metadata work per copy.

The full scan costs O(V polylog p). The exceptional flag scans and address
work cost O(M K0^2/B+M) in bit-volume units when R includes the B-bit record.
Their setup per coarse tile is absorbed by its N^g payload. This is not an
unpaid nonlinear boundary-signature evaluation on every payload bit.

## 5. Sparse radix gather and fixed-tape local processing

Within each *earlier-coordinate prefix fiber*, stable-radix sort the copies
by the displayed key, with unwrapped local coordinates in ordinary tensor
order. Only the g active axes occur in the key; all following spectator
coordinates remain one R-block payload. A radix pass scans each complete
header and payload, splits into two bucket tapes, concatenates, and resets
the same fixed set of tapes. Since K0=O(B), each pass costs O(M); K0 passes
cost O(M K0). No simultaneous open tape per tile, face or corner is needed.

Sorted copies form the exact input rectangles of section 3, consecutively.
Process one rectangle at a time. For each axis, expose its current local
coordinate field, apply the length-polynomial one-dimensional convolution,
and crop L positions from each end. Thus its length changes from its input
interval to the corresponding output interval. Other axes remain unchanged
until their own pass. This yields the tensor product of the restricted
one-dimensional maps, hence the exact desired face outputs.

Every current axis has length at most N+2L=poly(p). Its mixed-radix transpose
is the retained short-field construction: pad **only that field** to its
next power of two temporarily, move its O(log p) bits using O(log p) linear
block interchanges, remove the temporary padding, and use the correct new
field length on return. The temporary factor below two is removed before
the next axis. A rectangle therefore costs its volume times
`O(g polylog p)` for movement and unconditional polynomial-length arithmetic.
Summing over rectangles costs `O(M g polylog p)`. Signed/complex dyadic
convolution can use sign splitting and ordinary Kronecker packing with
O(p+log N)=O(p) guard bits, followed by the unconditional quasilinear integer
multiplier; no improved supplier is used on this sparse path.

After cropping, attach each output's physical coarse-tile and flat inner
address. Their keys are distinct because the face output partition is
disjoint. A second sparse radix sort orders them as holes in the retained
core-output stream. One merge scan replaces exactly those holes. The inverse
support-limited gather restores the original axis-major stream, including
the initially displaced coarse coordinates. All metadata is discarded.

## 6. Parameters for the proposed partial fusion

Use `d=p^epsilon`, `h=Theta(p/d)`, `g=p^(1-epsilon-zeta)` with fixed positive
zeta and epsilon>5/6. Suppose `L=O(p polylog p)` and take the dyadic side
`N=2^ceil((3/2)log2 p)`. The actual S_i eventually exceed every polynomial,
so N divides them and each periodic window is shorter than S_i.

Then `K0=O(p^(2(1-epsilon)-zeta) polylog p)` and `K0^2=o(p)`. The two sparse
cost multipliers satisfy

```
(gL/N) K0 = O(p^(5/2-3epsilon-2zeta) polylog p) = o(1),
(gL/N) g  = O(p^(3/2-2epsilon-2zeta) polylog p) = o(1).
```

All halo work is therefore O(V polylog p), below the desired
`O(V g^(1-a) polylog p)` routing term. The core convolution is
`O(V g^(1-q) polylog p)` since log N=Theta(log p).

The bounded-gauge condition cited in `PARTIAL-FUSION.md` remains payable:
with `a0=Theta(log d)` and theta=Theta(1/d), its variation is

```
g [a0 theta N + a0/theta]
 = O(p^(5/2-2epsilon-zeta) polylog p
      + p^(1-zeta) polylog p)
 = o(p)
```

for epsilon>5/6 and fixed zeta>0. Thus the larger polynomial tile does not
consume the O(p)-bit guard budget. This checks a layout/precision inequality;
it does not establish the missing Gaussian convolution factorization.

## Diagonal and factorization boundary

The theorem also applies to a fixed or polylogarithmic composition of these
translation-invariant convolutions and diagonal factors if every diagonal
scan/factor page has a proved sequential O(V polylog p) implementation and
all normalized tile-core and tile-halo values use O(p) bits. A tile-dependent
common scalar gauge may multiply every input to that tile and divide its
outputs; boundary copies must use the **destination** tile's gauge. No
enormous diagonal is formed and later canceled numerically by assertion.

A concrete sufficient diagonal implementation is available for
`D(x)=product_i d_i(x_i)`. Supply each one-axis factor page in coordinate
order, with all normalized prefix products bounded to O(p) bits. Traverse
the rectangle by nested coordinate loops and retain the g successive prefix
products on work tape. Multiply by the innermost factor once per record;
outer prefix updates occur once per complete inner row, then once per
complete inner rectangle, and so on. With side lengths at least two their
number is less than twice the record count. Singleton axes are folded into
one constant per rectangle. Rewinding a factor page costs its length and is
charged to the corresponding completed row. Ordinary O(p)-bit multiplication
therefore gives O(V polylog p) scan cost with O(gp) temporary bits. This
argument uses bounded normalized **prefix products**; bounds on the final
product alone do not suffice.

It does **not** cover an unbounded collection of different short kernels
inside one tile, a product-tree level with factor-two padding on all g axes,
or an unspecified transform-dependent sparse correction. Those require a
new representation theorem. In particular, the Gaussian_fast/product-tree
algorithm is not silently substituted for the translation-invariant kernel
assumed here.

## Finite evidence

`check_halo.py` verifies 5,632 exact outputs in three two/three-axis cyclic
examples, with asymmetric signed kernels, nontrivial diagonal conjugations,
periodic coarse carries, scrambled coarse order, unique sparse gather/scatter
keys and all local sequential crops. Pure flattening gives 3,040 wrong
boundary outputs across these examples; all are repaired. The exact copied
volumes equal `3V[(1+2L/N)^g-1]` in every case. These are constructive finite
controls; the preceding scan, metadata and volume arguments give the
conditional asymptotic claim.
